full_work.title: The Merchant of Moments
full_work.complete_text:
CRIER. Hear ye! Marrow the merchant buys your spare moments! Good prices paid in coin!
MARROW. Step up, step up! A minute here, an hour there - I'll take them off your hands.
PATIENCE. [aside] He buys what cannot be sold, and sells what cannot be bought.
WREN. I have a spare moment, sir - I was saving it for my garden.
MARROW. Sold! Here's a penny for it. Moments are moments.
HASTE. [rushing in] Take all of mine! I have no use for spare ones!
MARROW. Done and done. [to audience] See how they queue to be rid of time?
PATIENCE. Marrow, what will you do with a thousand borrowed minutes?
MARROW. Sell them back at interest, girl. Time is money, and money is mine.
CRIER. The merchant's vault is full! He owns a year of other people's afternoons!
WREN. But sir - my moment's gone, and my garden's unwatered, and somehow I am poorer.
HASTE. Mine too! I sold my moments and now I have no time to spend the money!
MARROW. [counting] A fortune in minutes... why do I feel I have nothing?
PATIENCE. Because a moment spent is not a moment lost - but a moment sold is a moment stolen from yourself.
MARROW. Then buy them back, I say! Name your price!
PATIENCE. They were never mine to sell, nor yours to keep. Spend them, Marrow - that is the only ownership time allows.
MARROW. [slowly] Then let the vault be opened. Take back your moments, all of you - and spend one, now, on something worth the spending.
ALL. [together] Time well spent is time well kept!
full_work.kind: Signature-original one-act morality play

full_work.title: The Garden of Good Intentions
full_work.complete_text:
GROVE. This spring I shall plant good intentions - rows and rows of them!
CARE. Then water them, Grove, and weed them, and tend them daily.
GROVE. Oh, intentions need no tending. Plant and forget, that's my way.
WEED. [creeping in] Did someone say... untended garden? How neighborly.
WEATHER. [blustering] And I shall rain when I please and shine when I please!
GROVE. See? The garden grows itself. [months pass] ...Why is it all weeds?
WEED. Your intentions were lovely seeds, Grove. Pity about the follow-through.
ROSE. [wilting] I was meant to be a kindness. Now I'm a rumor of one.
CARE. [entering with a watering can] Intentions are seeds, not harvests. Shall we begin again - properly?
GROVE. Is there still time?
CARE. There is always time for tending. But never time enough for neglecting.
GROVE. [kneeling] Then teach me, Care. Every row, every day.
WEED. [retreating] Tended gardens are no fun at all.
ALL. [together] Good intentions, daily tended, grow to harvest in the end!

full_work.complete_text:
JUDGE. Court is in session! The accused, Tomorrow, stands charged with never arriving.
YESTERDAY. [reading] The minutes show: promised daily, delivered never.
PATIENCE. I call the first witness - everyone who ever waited for tomorrow!
JURY. [murmuring] We waited... and waited...
TOMORROW. In my defense - I am always coming! I am the hope of every plan!
PATIENCE. Hope deferred makes the heart sick. What have you ever actually brought?
TOMORROW. Well... there was... hmm.
JUDGE. The court notes the accused's silence. Jury of Nows, how find you?
JURY. [together] We find for Today! Act now, and Tomorrow will take care of itself!
JUDGE. Sentence: Tomorrow is remanded to hope, and Today is awarded the verdict - use it well.
ALL. [together] Now is the time that time allows - spend Today, and end thy drowse!

full_work.title: The Clockmaker's Reckoning
full_work.complete_text:
COG. Fine clocks I make - and fine hours I sell! An hour of your life, sir? Only a memory!
HOUR. [knocking] Cog! I am come to collect. You sold three hundred hours you never lived.
COG. Sold? I merely... borrowed against the future.
MEMORY. [fading] And I am the price. Each hour you sold, I grow thinner.
APPRENTICE. Master, buy them back! Before Memory fades entirely!
COG. Buy back time? With what coin?
HOUR. With living, Cog. One lived hour repays one sold.
COG. Then I shall live them - every one! [He laughs, he weeps, he mends a toy, he watches a sunset.]
MEMORY. [growing clearer] Yes... yes, I remember now...
HOUR. The debt is paid. The clocks may tick again - but tick for the living now.
COG. Never again shall I sell an hour. I shall spend them - lavishly, and on purpose.
ALL. [together] Hours are for living, not for keeping - spend them well, and stop thy weeping!

full_work.complete_text:
COOK. The feast is laid! Two brothers inherit it equally.
MORE. [piling his plate] More! I must have more! It is never enough!
ENOUGH. [sharing his] Here, friend - have some of mine. There is plenty.
MORE. Fool! If you share, you'll have less!
ENOUGH. If I share, we'll both have enough. Watch.
HUNGER. [entering] I am Hunger, and I shall judge between you. Eat, both of you.
MORE. [eating frantically] Still... hungry... must have... more...
ENOUGH. [eating peacefully, sharing] I am satisfied - and so is everyone around me.
HUNGER. The verdict is plain: More is starving amid plenty; Enough is feasting amid sharing.
MORE. [ashamed] Teach me, brother.
ENOUGH. The secret is simple: enough is as good as a feast.
ALL. [together] Enough shared is a feast indeed - want no more than what you need!
